questions.knowledge_point: Computing Variance Given the Expected Value of a Random Variable and Its Square
questions.worked_solution:
We can compute the variance of a discrete random variable $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

Substituting the given values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\frac{2}{3}-{(\frac{1}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{9} \\  & =\frac{5}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Standard Deviation of a Random Variable
questions.problem: Let $X$ be the score obtained on the roll of a fair five-sided die with sides labeled with numbers $1$ through $5.$ What is $\text{SD}[X]?$
questions.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a random variable $X$ is defined as

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]},
$$

where the variance can be computed using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

First, we need to compute the probability mass function $f(x).$ Here, there are $5$ possible outcomes ($1,2,3,4,5$) and each outcome has the same probability, so the probability mass function is as follows:

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ |

Next, we compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3)+4\cdot f(4)+5\cdot f(5) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{5})+2(\frac{1}{5})+3(\frac{1}{5})+4(\frac{1}{5})+5(\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{3}^{2}\cdot f(3)+{4}^{2}\cdot f(4)+{5}^{2}\cdot f(5) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{5})+4(\frac{1}{5})+9(\frac{1}{5})+16(\frac{1}{5})+25(\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =11.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =11-{(3)}^{2} \\  & =11-9 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Standard Deviation of a Random Variable
questions.problem: Let $X$ be the score obtained on the roll of a fair eight-sided die with sides labeled with numbers $1$ through $8.$ What is $\text{SD}[X]?$
questions.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a random variable $X$ is defined as

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]},
$$

where the variance can be computed using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

First, we need to compute the probability mass function $f(x).$ Here, there are $8$ possible outcomes $(1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8)$ and each outcome has the same probability, so the probability mass function is as follows:

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ | $7$ | $8$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ |

Next, we compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3)+4\cdot f(4)+5\cdot f(5)+6\cdot f(6)+7\cdot f(7)+8\cdot f(8) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{8})+2(\frac{1}{8})+3(\frac{1}{8})+4(\frac{1}{8})+5(\frac{1}{8})+6(\frac{1}{8})+7(\frac{1}{8})+8(\frac{1}{8}) \\  & =\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{3}^{2}\cdot f(3)+{4}^{2}\cdot f(4)+{5}^{2}\cdot f(5)+{6}^{2}\cdot f(6)+{7}^{2}\cdot f(7)+{8}^{2}\cdot f(8) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{8})+4(\frac{1}{8})+9(\frac{1}{8})+16(\frac{1}{8})+25(\frac{1}{8})+36(\frac{1}{8})+49(\frac{1}{8})+64(\frac{1}{8}) \\  & =\frac{51}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{51}{2}-{(\frac{9}{2})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{51}{2}-\frac{81}{4} \\  & =\frac{21}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{21}{4}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{21}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing Variance Given a Probability Mass Function
questions.problem:
Let $X$ be the number obtained by a spinner with five sections labeled $1,5,10,15,20.$ The probability mass function $f(x)$ of $X$ is shown in the table below. What is $\text{Var}[X]?$

| $x$ | $1$ | $5$ | $10$ | $15$ | $20$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{5}{15}$ | $\frac{4}{15}$ | $\frac{3}{15}$ | $\frac{2}{15}$ | $\frac{1}{15}$ |
questions.worked_solution:
We can compute the variance of a discrete random variable $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

First, we compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =1\cdot f(1)+5\cdot f(5)+10\cdot f(10)+15\cdot f(15)+20\cdot f(20) \\  & =1(\frac{5}{15})+5(\frac{4}{15})+10(\frac{3}{15})+15(\frac{2}{15})+20(\frac{1}{15}) \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{5}^{2}\cdot f(5)+{10}^{2}\cdot f(10)+{15}^{2}\cdot f(15)+{20}^{2}\cdot f(20) \\  & =1(\frac{5}{15})+25(\frac{4}{15})+100(\frac{3}{15})+225(\frac{2}{15})+400(\frac{1}{15}) \\  & =\frac{251}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{251}{3}-{7}^{2} \\  & =\frac{251}{3}-49 \\  & =\frac{251}{3}-\frac{147}{3} \\  & =\frac{104}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
